cancellation_roles.description: Wire 4.1 check 8, 4.3, 4.8, spec 3.3: messages.json's payment_request_cancellation, as the shop signs it, without a label, presented with a certificate of the shop's keys (sender_cert) at a certificate of alice's wallet's keys (recipient_cert), each with its scopes changed, its permissions those Paykit's scopes need, and signed again. A cancellation's recipient holds the other role than its sender: the payer's goes from pay to request, the payee's from request to pay. accepted are the two pairings the recipient takes at check 8; refused are pay to pay and request to request, which it drops there. reason is paykit-lib's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

refused.reason: invalid: a cancellation's recipient doesn't hold the other role than its sender

refused.reason: invalid: a cancellation's recipient doesn't hold the other role than its sender

description: Every message kind as sent in v0.2 (Switch wire 4.5, wire 4): the exact JSON bytes, their BLAKE3 hash (refs, request hash), the sender app's signature over lp("pubky-switch/v1/msg", recipient identity, JSON), and the signed plaintext layout sender app ID (16) | signature (64) | u32_be(JSON length) | JSON, before zero padding. payment_request_labelled is sent by bob's hosted app under its label, and alice's acceptance of it copies the label; label_rejections holds requests a payer drops for their label; multi_protocol_senders holds messages from apps whose certificates hold another protocol's scopes; cancellation_roles holds a cancellation between certificates of each pair of roles.

label_rejections.description: Switch wire 5.1 checks 8 and 10, wire 4.1, 4.5, 4.6: payment_request messages a payer drops for their label, signed by bob's hosted app, whose certificate (the Switch set's documents.json) holds only request:shop1, each messages.json's payment_request_labelled with its label changed; alice's acceptance with a label that isn't valid, which bob's apps drop; and alice's acceptances a payee app drops at check 8 because its certificate (recipient_cert) doesn't hold their label: messages.json's payment_request_acceptance_labelled (label shop1) at an app holding only request:shop2, the hosted certificate with scopes changed and permissions derived, and the same acceptance without its label at the hosted app, which holds only request:shop1. A payer's reply with a label needs request or request:<label> for that label at the recipient; one without needs request. reason is the prototype's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

messages.name: payment_request
messages.note: One-time request with its destination (payment_endpoints) and a payment deadline.

messages.name: payment_request_required_app
messages.note: Request without a destination, payable only to the named payee app's endpoints.

messages.name: payment_request_recurring
messages.note: Monthly request anchored on January 31; later periods get their destination from period details.

messages.name: payment_request_acceptance
messages.note: Acceptance of the one-time request; refs name the request.

messages.name: payment_request_rejection
messages.note: Rejection with the optional v0.1 reason.

messages.name: payment_request_cancellation
messages.note: Payee cancellation of the recurring request.

messages.name: payment_period_details
messages.note: Destination and rates for the February period (anchor Jan 31, clamped to Feb 28).

messages.name: payment_proof
messages.note: Proof of the one-time request's attempt.

messages.name: payment_proof_period
messages.note: Payment of the February period by alice's wallet, in btc at the period details' rate (a manual payment: an Allowance pays only requests in its own asset); refs name the request and the period details it used.

messages.name: private_payment_list
messages.note: Private Payment List with one single-use and one reusable endpoint; version is the publishing time in ms; expires_at 30 days later (wire 4.13).

messages.name: payment_proof_unrequested
messages.note: Proof of a payment without a request, to the single-use list endpoint; no refs.

messages.name: payment_receipt
messages.note: Receipt for the one-time proof; refs name the proof, then the request.

messages.name: resend_request
messages.note: Ask for messages the sender's inbox accepted at one entry's acceptance time.

messages.name: resend_request_ids
messages.note: Ask for messages by msg_id.

messages.name: private_payment_list_request
messages.note: Ask the shop app for a newer list than the used one.

messages.name: allowance_proposal
messages.note: Allowee-authored proposal; terms as specs/allowances.md.

messages.name: allowance_acceptance
messages.note: Acceptance by the allower's executor app; executor_app_id is informational.

messages.name: allowance_rejection
messages.note: Rejection of another proposal (refs name that proposal).

messages.name: allowance_end
messages.note: End of the accepted Allowance; refs name the proposal and the acceptance.

messages.name: executor_notice
messages.note: Between own apps: the phone app ended the Allowance and tells the executor.

messages.name: resend_request_period
messages.note: Ask for the February period's messages of the recurring request: request_hashes names the request, billing_period the period, so the request itself isn't re-sent (wire 4.12).

messages.name: payment_request_labelled
messages.note: One-time request from bob's hosted app, which holds only request:shop1: it carries the signed label shop1, so the payer's replies go only to bob's apps holding request or request:shop1 (wire 4.5).

messages.name: payment_request_acceptance_labelled
messages.note: alice's acceptance of the labelled request: it copies the request's label (wire 4.6).

a resend_request from an app holding request and chat

multi_protocol_senders.description: Wire 4.1 check 8, spec 3.2, 3.3, Switch wire 3.1 "Several protocols": messages.json's payment_request and resend_request_ids, as the shop signs them, each presented with a certificate of the shop's keys that holds another protocol's scope, chat (sender_cert, documents.json multi_protocol_certificates), at alice's wallet (recipient_app), whose certificate is the Switch set's. Another protocol's scopes, and the switch permissions they bring, authorize no Paykit message: each kind still needs its Paykit scope, and a resend_request needs a Paykit App, one holding at least one Paykit scope. accepted are messages the wallet takes at check 8, from the shop holding request beside chat; refused are those it drops there, from the shop holding chat alone, a certificate Paykit's verifiers take. reason is paykit-lib's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

refused.reason: invalid: the sender's certificate holds no scope that sends the kind
